chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdul Kareem, from Ibn Abu Yafour, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who cut a finger of a woman. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His finger is cut until it reaches a third of the wergild (blood money). So when it exceeds the third, there is double (liability) for the man.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for compensating a cut finger according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money) for amputating a woman's finger, establishing a proportional compensation system where the penalty scales with the extent of the injury. It highlights the Shia scholarly principle of precise quantification in bodily injuries, noting that once the injury surpasses one-third of the total *diyah*, the liability doubles, reflecting a nuanced approach to partial damages distinct from full compensation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdul Kareem, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who cut a finger of a woman. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His finger would be cut until it ends up to a third of the wergild. So when it exceeds the third, there would be double regarding the man’.
